newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures were called to open little changed Tuesday as traders expected the market to consolidate near current levels after eight consecutive sessions of losses.

Speculative liquidation continued to pressure New York raws Monday, amid a lack of physical interest. CSCE March world sugar ended down 0.15 cent at 10.49 cents a lb after trading down to a session low of 10.44 cents.
On the charts, traders pegged near-term support at 10.45 cents. Resistance was noted at 10.57-10.60 cents.

Fundamentally, German statistician F.O. Licht said news that Philippine 1996/97 sugar production would be lower than expected would have no discernable market impact due to the high level of imports in 1995/96.
"Even if the crop should be around last year's level of 1.8 million tonnes, imports are likely to fall drastically in 1996/97," Licht said in its daily report.
Philippine Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) cut its production estimate for 1996/97 (September/August) to 1.8 million tonnes, raw value, down from earlier forecasts of around 2.0 million tonnes.
In London, LIFFE white sugar futures were firmer early Tuesday in quiet trade. March sugar was up 0.40 cents, to $300.50, and the back months were flat to 60 cents higher, at 0907 EST/1407 GMT.

On the physical side, Libya tendered to buy two cargoes of 45 ICUMSA white sugar for February/March shipment and Iran was also looking for a similar cargo for the same shipment period as part of its continued buying programme.
Turkish state refiner Turkseker said it was still assessing bids from around 10 companies for a tender under which it will sell up to 50,000 tonnes of white sugar.
